Let me analyze this conflict.

Register applicant: "Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH"
Document applicant: "Mettler Toledo"

The document says "Applicant: Mettler Toledo" followed by address "Heuwinkelstrasse, 8606 Nänikon, Switzerland". The document's text appears truncated — the applicant field in the document says "Mettler Toledo" (likely "Mettler-Toledo GmbH" or the full name was cut off in extraction — actually the text shows "**Applicant** Mettler Toledo Heuwinkelstrasse, 8606 Nänikon, Switzerland **Manufacturer** Met" — the document itself may have the applicant as "Mettler Toledo" with address, and the extraction may have truncated). Actually wait — the extracted context is the certificate's own text. The document applicant reads "Mettler Toledo" with Swiss address (Nänikon — that's Mettler-Toledo's Swiss address, Mettler-Toledo GmbH Switzerland). The register says "Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH" which is also a Mettler-Toledo entity (Engineering Labs, based in Nänikon/ Greifensee, Switzerland).

Is "Mettler Toledo" the same entity as "Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH"? The document shows only "Mettler Toledo" — possibly truncated in extraction ("**Manufacturer** Met" suggests truncation of the document text at the end). The applicant line reads "Mettler Toledo Heuwinkelstrasse, 8606 Nänikon, Switzerland". Hmm, actually NMi certificates often list applicant as "Mettler-Toledo AG" or similar. The extracted text shows "Mettler Toledo" as applicant — this could be a truncated extraction. But per the task, we take document as "Mettler Toledo".

Verdict options:
- same-entity: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences. "Mettler Toledo" vs "Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH" — is this legal-suffix drift? "Mettler Toledo" is missing "Engineering Labs GmbH". That's more than a suffix drift — it's a shortened name. However, both plausibly refer to the same corporate family and possibly the same entity. The address Nänikon, Switzerland matches Mettler-Toledo's Swiss operations. "Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH" is indeed located in Nänikon/Greifensee Switzerland? Actually Mettler-Toledo GmbH, Im Langacher 44, 8606 Greifensee... Heuwinkelstrasse is in Nänikon. Mettler-Toledo's weighing technologies... The register name "Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH" — hmm.

But per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity". Is "Mettler Toledo" genuinely a different company from "Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH"? They're not genuinely different companies — the document shows a truncated/abbreviated form. But strictly, the document says "Mettler Toledo" which is incomplete, not a different entity. The missing "Engineering Labs GmbH" is a truncation artifact.

Hmm, which category? The rule for same-entity covers "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences". "Mettler Toledo" vs "Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH" — the hyphen drop is spelling drift; the missing "Engineering Labs GmbH" is truncation, not exactly legal-suffix drift. But it's clearly the same corporate entity being referred to (applicant Mettler Toledo at Nänikon, Switzerland; register's Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH is a Swiss entity of the same group). The document extraction seems truncated overall ("Manufacturer Met" cut off), suggesting "Mettler Toledo" may itself be truncated.

Best value for fused record: register's canonical form "Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH" if same-entity (rules say for same-entity we'd prefer... actually the rules don't explicitly say which value for same-entity, but register canonical form makes sense; "document-noise" explicitly says best_value from the register).

Alternatively, verdict "document-noise" — the document's "Mettler Toledo" is an extraction truncation artifact. The rule says "Extraction artifacts (address fragments glued into a name, obvious OCR noise) = document-noise with best_value from the register." Truncation could be an extraction artifact. But is it "obvious"? The document text itself might genuinely say "Mettler Toledo" — but NMi certificates typically give full legal names. Given the visible truncation of the document text at "**Manufacturer** Met", it's plausible the whole document context is truncated. Hmm, but "**Applicant** Mettler Toledo Heuwinkelstrasse..." — the applicant section seems complete (name, then address, then next section header). So the document itself might list "Mettler Toledo" (without hyphen and without GmbH) — actually many NMi certs list "Mettler-Toledo" as applicant without suffix.

I think the best verdict is "same-entity": hyphen/spelling drift ("Mettler Toledo" vs "Mettler-Toledo"), same corporate family, address confirms Swiss Mettler-Toledo entity; the register carries the full legal name. Best value: register's canonical full form "Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH".

Hmm, but one could argue "Engineering Labs" is a distinct subsidiary. Mettler-Toledo Engineering Labs GmbH? Let me think — Mettler-Toledo has "Mettler-Toledo GmbH" in Greifensee, "Mettler-Toledo International Inc" etc. The register value is authoritative per OIML-CS database. The document's abbreviated name doesn't denote a genuinely different company — it's a loose reference to the same applicant group. Verdict same-entity, best_value register form.

Why sentence: "Both refer to the same Mettler-Toledo applicant; the document shows a hyphen-dropped, truncated rendering while the register holds the full legal name."
